newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds open stronger on broad-based buying.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds open stronger on broad-based buying.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened stronger on broad-based buying on Thursday, with the market extending gains made after yesterday's successful 10-year bond auction.

"There was some overseas buying and we're seeing some more good follow through in the long end here this morning. The general view was that yesterday's 10-year was decently received in Canada," said Hank Cunningham, director of fixed-income with First Marathon Securities Ltd.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.40 to C$120.82 to yield 6.422 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 7/32 to yield 6.47 percent. The negative spread between the bonds widened to five basis points from three basis points at Wednesday's close.

The Canadian government's sale yesterday of C$2.3 billion of 6.0 percent bonds due June 1, 2008 produced a high low gap of 1.7 basis points and a tail of 0.8 percent, reflecting firm buying interest, analysts said.

Canadian bonds also benefited from gains this morning in U.S. Treasuries, which were stronger following a report showing new U.S. jobless claims totaled 300,000 in the week ended August 2, up from 275,000 a week earlier.

Analysts said recent weakness in the currency was also having an impact on prices. While the dollar traded flat overnight, it weakened sharply yesterday to close at C$1.3875 (US$0.7207) from Tuesday's close at C$1.3800 (US$0.7246).

"There is some scuttlebutt now circulating that the Bank (of Canada) may have to move rates up here sooner than he would like to, especially if tomorrow's employment report shows a very vigorous employment situation in Canada," said Cunningham.
Statistics Canada tomorrow will report its employment data for July.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.15 to C$109.75 to yield 5.922 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond rose 4/32 to yield 6.18 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 26 basis points from 27 basis points at Wednesday's close.
